key_insight: Learned diffusion proposals help continuous constraint solving only in narrow regimes; for many systems, budget-matched random multi-start is just as good or better once exact polishing and checking are included.
engineering_relevance: For solver design, the main gain from learning may lie in discrete repair/augmentation selection, while value assignment often remains competitive with simpler randomized search under the same compute budget.
method: Model the constraint problem as a factor graph and use a graph-neural diffusion denoiser to propose continuous assignments.
Polish each proposal with descent on an exact computer-algebra energy, then certify with an exact symbolic checker.
Compare against matched random multi-start baselines and a candidate-conditioned repair ranker over the same refinement budget.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that random multi-start matches learned proposals in trapped low-dimensional cases, dominates in high dimension, and that a simple best-of-K formula accurately predicts success across curves with mean absolute error 0.012.
watch_item: The learned advantage appears regime-dependent and can disappear when variables are strongly coupled, so evaluation must include a strict random-restart control under identical polishing and checking budgets.
paper_title: When Do Learned Diffusion Proposals Help Constraint Solving? A Controlled Study on Continuous Algebraic Systems
